overview: The 28BYJ-48 is the beginner's stepper motor: cheap, slow, and low-torque, but capable of precise, repeatable positioning that a plain DC motor can't do — tell it to turn exactly 45 degrees and it will, every time, with no feedback sensor needed. It's unipolar and needs more current than a microcontroller pin can supply, so it's always sold with a small blue ULN2003 driver board that takes 4 logic-level inputs and switches the motor's coils. The internal ~64:1 gear reduction is why it's simultaneously very precise and very slow — great for a camera pan mechanism, useless for anything needing speed.
simpleSummary: A cheap motor that turns in tiny, exact steps instead of spinning freely, so it can go to precise positions.

specifications.stepAngle: 5.625°/64 per motor step (~2048 steps per output shaft revolution after gearing)
specifications.torque: Low (a few N·cm) — precise but weak
specifications.driverBoard: ULN2003 Darlington transistor array (required — cannot be driven directly from a microcontroller pin)

pinMap.name: IN1
pinMap.function: Driver board input controlling coil phase 1.
pinMap.currentLimit: Logic-level only (driver board handles motor current)
pinMap.gotcha: Stepping sequence matters — driving IN1-IN4 out of the correct order causes the motor to buzz and vibrate without turning.

pinMap.name: IN2
pinMap.function: Driver board input controlling coil phase 2.

pinMap.name: IN3
pinMap.function: Driver board input controlling coil phase 3.

pinMap.name: IN4
pinMap.function: Driver board input controlling coil phase 4.

pinMap.name: Driver VCC
pinMap.function: Power input for the motor coils, feeds through the ULN2003 board.
pinMap.gotcha: Powering multiple steppers from a microcontroller's onboard 5V pin can brown it out — use a separate supply for more than one.

pinMap.name: Driver GND
pinMap.function: Ground reference, shared with the controlling microcontroller.

useCases.title: Camera pan mechanism
useCases.scenario: Precisely rotate a camera or sensor mount to an exact angle and hold position.

useCases.title: Small indexing/sorting mechanism
useCases.scenario: Rotate a small turntable to exact positions for sorting or dispensing.

useCases.title: Clock or gauge mechanism
useCases.scenario: Drive an analog-style pointer or clock hand with repeatable precision.

oftenConfusedWith: NEMA 17 (bipolar, far more torque and speed, needs a proper stepper driver)
oftenUpgradedTo: NEMA 17 with an A4988/DRV8825 driver, once torque or speed becomes a limitation
